body.statement: For a rational polynomial system with at most \(s_G\) equalities and weak inequalities, degree at most \(D_G\), coefficient bit length \(O(B)\), and \(k_G\) quantified variables, one-block real quantifier elimination decides feasibility and computes a one-free-variable projection using \(B^{O(1)}(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\) bit operations.  The univariate output degrees are \(D_G^{O(k_G)}\), their coefficient bit lengths are \(B(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\), and nonempty sign cells admit exact real-algebraic sample points within the same asymptotic bounds.

source.locator: Theorems 1.3.1 and 1.3.3, pp. 1003--1005, together with the well-behaved-algorithm and sample-point bounds in Sections 1.2 and 3
source.verbatim_statement: there exists an equivalent quantifier-free formula ... and the degrees of the polynomials P_ij(y) are bounded by d^{Π_i O(k_i)}

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-09 against the JACM article PDF uploaded by coauthor Richard Pollack at ResearchGate and mirrored by CiteSeerX (DOI 10.1145/235809.235813): Theorem 1.3.1 on pp.1004-1005 gives quantifier-free output, output-degree and arithmetic-operation bounds; the well-behaved definition on p.1004 gives integer intermediate/output bit-size control; Theorem 1.3.3 on p.1005 gives existential decision arithmetic complexity; Section 3.1.3 on pp.1028-1029 constructs univariate-representation points meeting every sign cell with degree/arithmetic and integer coefficient-size bounds. The source states arithmetic-operation complexity plus bit-size growth; any claimed bit-operation form is a derived corollary and must be reviewed as such, not attributed verbatim.
